messages:
maria: Hey team — ran into a thing where automatic fallback flipped traffic for a customer after 3 transient 502s and they ended up with lower-quality completions. Need a UX + telemetry pattern to help debugging and make the policy decisions more transparent. Can we spec an 'Inspector' panel that shows the actual trigger events, sampled requests, and the policy evaluation chain?

kevin: +1. Current logs just give event IDs and an opaque reason code. Hard to correlate to policy logic. :confused:

anya: Prototype idea: policy trace view that shows a timeline of decision points (events, rule evaluations), sampled request payloads (redacted by default), chosen model variant, and the metric snapshots that caused the rule to fire.

sam: We need a clear privacy model — who can see samples, and how do we redact? Also retention/DB cost concerns.

maria: Agreed. Default to strict redaction; expose a 'request full payload' flow that creates an audit ticket and requires justification.

deploybot: Deploybot: rollout/autofallback-inspector v0.1 deployed to staging at 1749991125

kevin: UX idea: small inline badge on the policy row "Why it fired" that opens a right-hand panel. Panel tabs: Events, Samples, Policy Eval, Telemetry. Each tab has time filters and links to raw logs.

anya: Also a sandbox 'replay' button to re-evaluate a saved request against the policy rules (read-only, runs in a sandboxed evaluator).

sam: Sampling budget — we can't keep full samples for every customer. Propose per-customer sampling cap + retention TTL + an org-level opt-in for longer retention.

maria: Proposed defaults: 5 samples per customer per hour, 24h retention, opt-in for 7d. Document in Console > Settings > Telemetry.

kevin: Minimal config sketch to discuss with infra:
```
policy:
  id: auto-fallback-1
  conditions:
    - name: error_spike
      expr: "error_rate(window=5m) > 0.03"
    - name: p50_latency
      expr: "latency.p50(window=10m) > 200"
  sampling:
    samples_per_customer_per_hour: 5
    retention_hours: 24
```

anya: Good. Also show an immediate human-readable: "Fired because error_rate(5m)=4.7% > 3% and p50 latency(10m)=215ms > 200ms" — helps non-engineers.

sam: For redaction: strip user identifiers and free-text fields, keep model inputs tokens length + top-level metadata. If an operator requests full payload a soft audit ticket is created. Make sure KMS keys and access controls are enforced.

maria: Action items: kevin — build panel shell + policy-trace API; anya — wireframe panel and humanized messages; sam — draft privacy/retention doc and RBAC constraints; i'll sync with infra re: storage and TTLs. Owners: kevin/anya/sam/maria.

kevin: I'll start a short RFC and link it here with API proto and storage estimate.

incidentbot: IncidentBot: linked alert IR-904 (502 spike) — added context for the top event in the trace.

anya: One more UX thought — surface an estimated cost delta if we had stayed on primary model vs fallback for the sampled window. It helps product owners tune thresholds if the fallback is too conservative.

maria: Love that. Ok team — let's meet Thursday 10am to review the prototype and RFC. :calendar: 

kevin: thumbs up. I'll add the meeting and include a short recording of the staging flow for folks who can't make it. :+1:
